correctness.rationale: The actual generator calculation gives exterior quadratic-variation limit c_pi^(-2ell) and decaying transformed drift. A smooth flat-interior cutoff controls quadratic variation globally, proving the sharp Gaussian upper exponent. A Brownian bridge event staying above a fixed lower barrier and above the target level after near-full time forces no return to the interior and yields the matching sharp exponent; positivity of locally elliptic paths transfers from a distant annulus to any initial state. Tonelli converts the logarithmic tail into strict exponential-moment finiteness/divergence. The equality coefficient and full density prefactors are not claimed. The 603 exact-rational test assertions independently cross-check elementary power cancellations, not the infinite stochastic argument.

value.rationale: The critical-power moment endpoint of the motivating diffusion theorem gave only a small-time finite bound and a separated large-time infinite bound. The exact Weibull cost resolves the intrinsic sharp strict time boundary for every subcritical temperature, all dimensions, and all target functions satisfying the same asymptotic conditions. The result identifies a distributional constant not determined by qualitative ergodic rates, and it supplies a reusable radial-clock proof technique. It is not a routine parameter substitution, numeric recomputation, or claim of a density prefactor.
